title: SECTION 1, UNIT 2
subtitle: Differentiate critical antineoplastics and high-risk look-alikes (CARBOplatin/CISplatin, vinBLAStine/vinCRIStine, epiNEPHrine/ePHEDrine) using verified Tall Man lettering.

lasaPairs.feature: Severe hypoglycemia in non-diabetic patients or uncontrolled intraocular pressure/acid-base imbalance.
Dramatically different dosing schedules; cisplatin dosed at carboplatin levels causes fatal nephrotoxicity, neurotoxicity, and ototoxicity.
Severe toxicity, fluid retention, neuropathy, and neutropenia due to differing dosing frequencies and premedication protocols.
Dosing regimen errors leading to irreversible, cumulative cardiotoxicity and severe myelosuppression.
Vincristine is dosed in fractions of the dose of vinblastine; administering vinblastine doses using vincristine causes fatal neurotoxicity.
Subtherapeutic resuscitation in anaphylaxis/cardiac arrest, or extreme hypertension and tachyarrhythmia from incorrect potency delivery.
Severe precipitous hypotension, reflex tachycardia, or cerebral ischemia due to formulation and pharmacokinetic mismatches.
Hyperkalemia and dehydration vs. unmanaged hypertension or peripheral edema.
Unmanaged neuropathic pain, differences in discontinuation syndrome, or heightened risk of serotonergic excess.
Severe anticholinergic side effects, abrupt discontinuation syndrome with missed paroxetine, and drug-drug metabolic interactions.
Extrapyramidal symptoms, severe sedation, or metabolic syndrome in a patient merely requiring acid suppression.
Severe bone marrow ablation/failure vs. acute transplant rejection or uncontrolled autoimmune flare.
